learning_outcomes.text: Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools in their professional activities.
Know and apply the knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and capabilities for the application of materials engineering.

syllabus_topics: Melting of alloys. Casting. Molds and Ingots. Characteristic periods in mold solidification.
Shrinkage and grain shape in each zone.
Internal stresses and external and internal cracks.
Procedures to avoid or reduce defects.
Lines and planes of maximum atomic density (Miller indices).
General state of stress. Stress tensor. Critical shear stress.
Deformation by: Translation and Twinning. Dislocations.
Plastic and elastic deformation in polycrystals.
Effects of heating on plastic deformations.
Strain hardening and Annealing heat treatment against strain hardening.
Summary of treatments and their effects.
Effects of temperature and time on tempering.
FUNDAMENTALS OF HEAT TREATMENTS OF STEELS
Austenite transformations: "S" curve or TTT diagram.
Types of cooling: Slow cooling; Intermediate cooling; Rapid cooling.
Isothermal transformations of austenite. Formation of pearlite, bainite and martensite. Properties obtained.
Austenitization heating. Transformations of steel constituents into austenite.
Austenite grain growth. Overheated and burnt steel.
Types of annealing: Homogenization, Regeneration, Softening, Spheroidizing, Recrystallization, Stress stabilization, Isothermal.
Complete austenitization quenching / Incomplete austenitization quenching.
Severity of quench. Variations in cooling rate depending on the cooling medium and temperature. Choice of cooling medium.
Hardenability. Critical diameter and Ideal critical diameter.
Jominy test. Theoretical calculation of the Jominy curve.
Interrupted quenching, Surface hardening, Induction hardening.
Carburizing. Factors influencing the process. Properties obtained.
Nitriding. Factors influencing the process. Properties obtained.
Alphagenic, gammagenic, carbon-forming or graphite-forming elements.
Austenitic, ferritic, martensitic and cementitic steels.
Influence of Nickel, Manganese, Silicon, Chromium, Molybdenum, Tungsten, Vanadium, Cobalt, Titanium, Aluminum and Boron on the properties of steels.
Effects of alloying elements on pearlitic and bainitic transformations depending on whether they form carbides or not. Action during tempering. Secondary hardness.
Effects of alloying elements on martensitic transformations. Retained austenite.
Stainless steels. Iron-chromium Diagram. Influence of Nickel. Schaeffler Diagram.
Tool steels. High-speed steels. Specific treatments for high-speed steels.
Magnesium, Beryllium, Titanium. Properties and applications.
Copper. Copper alloys: bronzes and brasses. Classification and treatments. Aluminum bronzes.
Lead, Tin, Zinc, Antimony, Nickel, Cobalt, Manganese, Chromium, Molybdenum, Tungsten, alloys of these metals. Properties and applications.
Principles of the Selection Method. Structuring of Databases and Data Tables.
Exploring Databases. General and Advanced Databases.
Specific Databases: Elements, Materials Science and Engineering, Products-Materials-Processes
Data Tables: Materials, Processes, Geometries, Suppliers, References,...
Material Selection using filters in links between Data Tables.
Material Selection combining different types of Selection stages.
Selection, Filtering and Classification of Materials using Material Indices.
Advanced practical cases of Material Selection. Conflicting objectives.
assessment_rules: The course can be passed through progressive evaluation or a global exam. For progressive evaluation, the final grade is calculated as 42.5% for the First Progressive Test, 42.5% for the Second Progressive Test, and 15% for the Laboratory Practical Test. For this path, the minimum grade for each progressive theory/problems control must be at least 4/10, the average of the two controls must be at least 5/10, and the overall weighted grade must be at least 5/10. For the global exam path, the Global Theory and Problems Test accounts for 85%, and the Laboratory Practical Test for 15%. To pass, each part of the global test must be at least 4/10, the average of its two parts at least 5/10, and the overall weighted grade at least 5/10. The laboratory practical test is mandatory and non-recoverable; non-attendance without justification leads to a maximum final grade of 4/10. Parts of the theory/problems block passed with 5/10 or more are "liberated" for the ordinary and extraordinary calls of the current academic year; the highest grade is kept if re-evaluated. The laboratory grade (5/10 or more) is retained for subsequent calls and enrollments as long as the study plan doesn't change. If any minimum grade requirement is not met, the maximum final grade will be 4/10.
